facts.statement: Brachylophosaurus is a genus of dinosaur.
facts.quote: taxon: Brachylophosaurus

facts.statement: Brachylophosaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Late Cretaceous,

facts.statement: Brachylophosaurus was first named by Charles Mortram Sternberg in 1953.
facts.quote: authority: Sternberg, 1953

facts.statement: The type species of Brachylophosaurus is Brachylophosaurus canadensis.
facts.quote: type_species: Brachylophosaurus canadensis

facts.statement: The type specimen of Brachylophosaurus was discovered in 1936 in the Oldman Formation of Alberta, Canada.
facts.quote: It was first named in 1953 by Charles Mortram Sternberg for a skull and skeleton he discovered in 1936 in the Oldman Formation of Alberta, Canada

facts.statement: A bonebed containing 800 specimens of Brachylophosaurus was found in the Judith River Formation of Montana.
facts.quote: extensive discoveries in the Judith River Formation of Montana, USA have uncovered not only additional skulls and skeletons with extensive impressions of skin, but also a bonebed of 800 specimens

facts.statement: John R. Horner named a Montana specimen Brachylophosaurus goodwini.
facts.quote: The earliest of these discoveries in Montana was named Brachylophosaurus goodwini by John R. Horner

facts.statement: It is debated whether Brachylophosaurus goodwini is a synonym of B. canadensis or a distinct member of the Brachylophosaurini tribe.
facts.quote: it is now believed that there was only a single species of Brachylophosaurus, with B. goodwini as either a junior synonym of B. canadensis or an indeterminate member of Brachylophosaurini

facts.statement: The type specimen CMN 8893 was collected by Charles Mortram Sternberg in 1936 from Dinosaur Provincial Park, Alberta.
facts.quote: In 1936, American paleontologist Charles Mortram Sternberg led an expedition of the Geological Survey of Canada to the region of Dinosaur Provincial Park, Alberta, collecting multiple specimens for the Canadian Museum of Nature including a skull and partial skeleton of a hadrosaur (CMN 8893)

facts.statement: The quarry where the type specimen was found was lost for over 20 years before being rediscovered in 2001 and designated Q103.
facts.quote: Sternberg labelled this quarry, near Steveville, Alberta, as quarry No. 58, and though he marked it with a stake and identified it on a map, it was lost for more than 20 years as the back wall had collapsed and buried the marker, only being rediscovered in 2001 and officially designated Q103

facts.statement: Sternberg classified Brachylophosaurus canadensis within the subfamily Hadrosaurinae.
facts.quote: As such, in 1953 Sternberg named CMN 8893 Brachylophosaurus canadensis, identifying it as a relative of all aforementioned hadrosaurs within the subfamily Hadrosaurinae

facts.statement: The genus name Brachylophosaurus means "short-crested lizard" in Ancient Greek.
facts.quote: The genus name comes from the Ancient Greek words βραχύς (brakhús), meaning "short", λόφος (lóphos), meaning "crest", and σαῦρος (saûros), meaning "lizard"

facts.statement: John R. Horner named the second species Brachylophosaurus goodwini in 1998 based on a specimen from Montana.
facts.quote: A second species of Brachylophosaurus was named in 1998 by American paleontologist John R. Horner, for a specimen found in the Judith River Formation of Montana

facts.statement: A third specimen, FMNH PR 862, was discovered on September 9, 1922 by George Fryer Sternberg.
facts.quote: FMNH PR 862 was found on September 9, 1922 by George Fryer Sternberg, brother of Charles M. Sternberg

facts.statement: Specimen FMNH PR 862 was uncatalogued at the Field Museum until 1972.
facts.quote: It was uncatalogued at the Field Museum until 1972 when it received the number FMNH PR 862

facts.statement: A well-preserved specimen TMP 1990.104.1 was found in southern Alberta near Manyberries and Onefour.
facts.quote: a second well-preserved specimen has been found in southern Alberta in the area of Manyberries and Onefour, collected by the Royal Tyrrell Museum of Paleontology as TMP 1990.104.1

facts.statement: A maxilla from the upper Wahweap Formation of Utah has been tentatively attributed to Brachylophosaurus.
facts.quote: A single maxilla from the upper Wahweap Formation of Utah has been tentatively attributed to Brachylophosaurus based on greater similarity than other hadrosaurines, and its equivalent age to material from Judith River

facts.statement: Specimens MOR 794 and MOR 1071 were found 27 km north of Malta, Montana, and 87 km south of the Canadian border.
facts.quote: The individual skeleton (MOR 794) and bonebed (MOR 1071) are from stratigraphically equivalent sites 27 km north of Malta, Montana, and 87 km south of the Canadian border

facts.statement: Skeleton MOR 794 was discovered in 1994 by Nate Murphy 15 miles north of Malta.
facts.quote: MOR 794 was discovered in 1994 by fossil collector Nate Murphy on a hillside 15 mi north of Malta, preserved in three dimensions without any flattening

facts.statement: A specimen nicknamed "Leonardo" was discovered in 2000 during an expedition led by Nate Murphy.
facts.quote: Another specimen of Brachylophosaurus was discovered during an expedition led by Murphy in 2000, and given the nickname "Leonardo"

facts.statement: The "Leonardo" specimen was identified by the Guinness Book of World Records as the "Best Preserved Dinosaur".
facts.quote: The preservation resulted in Guiness Book of World Records identifying "Leonardo" as the "Best Preserved Dinosaur"

facts.statement: The juvenile specimen nicknamed "Peanut" was discovered in 2002 by Robert E. Buresh and Andrew Kantor.
facts.quote: "Peanut" was discovered in 2002 by Robert E. Buresh and Andrew Kantor while part of a summer dinosaur dig run by the institute

facts.statement: A skeleton dubbed "Marco" was discovered in May 2008 by Steven Cowan.
facts.quote: In May 2008, Steven Cowan, public-relations coordinator at the Houston Museum of Natural Science, discovered a Brachylophosaurus skeleton subsequently dubbed "Marco" from the same area as Leonardo

facts.statement: Brachylophosaurus had a distinctive flat, paddle-like bony crest on the back of its skull.
facts.quote: Brachylophosaurus is notable for its bony crest, which forms a horizontally flat, paddle-like plate over the top of the rear skull.

facts.statement: Adult Brachylophosaurus reached a length of at least 9 meters.
facts.quote: Brachylophosaurus was a typical hadrosaur which reached an adult length of at least 9 m.

facts.statement: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimated the maximum length of Brachylophosaurus at 11 meters and its weight at 7 metric tons.
facts.quote: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimated maximum length at 11 m resulting in weight of 7 MT.

facts.statement: Brachylophosaurus possessed cheek pouches to hold food and dental batteries containing hundreds of stacked teeth.
facts.quote: Like other hadrosaurs, Brachylophosaurus had features like cheeks to keep fodder in the mouth and dental batteries with hundreds of stacked teeth.

facts.statement: In adults, the nasal crest was flat and paddle-shaped, largely or totally overhanging the supratemporal fenestrae.
facts.quote: The crest formed by the nasal bones is flat and paddle-shaped in adult individuals and largely or totally overhangs the supratemporal fenestrae.

facts.statement: The crest of Brachylophosaurus was solid massive bone rather than hollow.
facts.quote: The crest is not hollow but consists of massive bone.

facts.statement: The upper jaw bone (maxilla) was elongated in the front section.
facts.quote: The maxilla, the tooth-bearing upper jaw bone, is rather elongated in front.

facts.statement: Brachylophosaurus had teeth stacked in batteries with up to three teeth per position.
facts.quote: The teeth are stacked in a tooth battery, with up to three teeth per position.

facts.statement: Soft tissue casts on Brachylophosaurus fossils generally lay close to the bones, likely due to desiccation or sediment compression.
facts.quote: Generally, the surface is close to the bones, which could be caused by desiccation before burial or the compressive action of the covering sediment.

facts.statement: A soft tissue cast of Brachylophosaurus revealed muscles about six centimeters thick around the right shoulder.
facts.quote: An exception is the region around the right shoulder, which shows the profile of about six centimetres thick muscles.

facts.statement: The second, third, and fourth fingers of Brachylophosaurus were encased in a shared soft tissue sheath resembling a mitten.
facts.quote: The second, third and fourth finger of the hand are contained in a shared soft tissue "mitten".

facts.statement: A famous Brachylophosaurus specimen named 'Leonardo' showed evidence of parasitism by small, needle-like worms with fine bristles in its stomach.
facts.quote: Examination of the stomach of "Leonardo" also reveals that the dinosaur was parasitized by small, needle-like worms covered in fine bristles.

facts.statement: Despite examining over 10,000 fossils, tumors were found only in Brachylophosaurus and closely related genera.
facts.quote: Although more than 10,000 fossils were examined in this manner, the tumors were limited to Brachylophosaurus and closely related genera.

facts.statement: Brachylophosaurus was a generalist herbivore that acted as both a browser and grazer, but primarily browsed based on stomach contents.
facts.quote: The study also found that Brachylophosaurus was a generalist herbivore; being both a browser and a grazer, but it did more of the former rather than the latter due to the contents found in its stomach.

facts.statement: Brachylophosaurus lived during the Campanian stage, between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Brachylophosaurus belongs to the subfamily Brachylophosaurini.
facts.quote: Parent group: Brachylophosaurini

facts.statement: Brachylophosaurus is classified in the family Hadrosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Hadrosauridae

facts.statement: Brachylophosaurus is a member of the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: It is debated whether the crest was used for pushing contests, as some researchers suggest it but others doubt it was strong enough.
facts.quote: Some researchers suggest it was used for pushing contests, but it may not have been strong enough for this.

facts.statement: Brachylophosaurus fossils in the Dinosaur Park Formation may represent individuals that died while migrating through the region.
facts.quote: Some of the less common hadrosaurs in the Dinosaur Park Formation of Dinosaur Provincial Park like Brachylophosaurus may represent the remains of individuals who died while migrating through the region.

facts.statement: Brachylophosaurus may have inhabited upland areas where it nested or fed.
facts.quote: They might also have had a more upland habitat where they may have nested or fed.
